newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Curacao refinery to run 105,000 bpd from Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Curacao refinery to run 105,000 bpd from Saturday.

text.p: The fire-hit 310,000 barrel per day (bpd) Curacao oil refinery operated by Petroleos de Venezuela expects to increase its crude oil throughput by 45,000 bpd to 105,000 bpd within two days, a refinery official said Thursday.
The largest crude distillation tower at the plant was struck by a fire on Thursday morning, cutting refinery throughput by 130,000 bpd.

The refinery was still running 60,000 bpd through crude unit number two after number three was disabled by the fire, but the official expected the refinery to average 105,000 bpd throughput in August.

"We can put some additional 45,000 bpd in another unit -- a thermal cracker that we are going to convert into a crude distiller. We are going to do that today and tomorrow. On Saturday certainly we will be running 105,000 bpd," he said.
"The crude imports were planned to be 168,000 bpd next month and we think it will become 105,000 bpd. And we are looking for some additional heavy crude to go to 120,000 bpd," he added.
He said the fire was extinguished at 9.30 am local time and there were no injuries.

"Immediately there will be no effect on our deliveries," he continued. "We have sufficient in stock to be able to deliver to our clients, but if we are not on stream soon, we might have to import some components from our affiliates in Venezuela to manufacture gasoline. We are thinking about importing naphtha to increase the octane number."
He said it would take several days to discover the extent of the damage.
The Curacao refinery is rented by Petroleos de Venezuela on 20 year contract and is a major supplier of refined oil products for the United States market.
